result.title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning
result.summary: Inferring the unseen side of a 3D assembly requires reasoning about part placement and occlusion. Different assemblies can match the observed views while producing different hidden views, leaving the target ambiguous. We introduce SixthView, a benchmark in which models predict a sixth orthographic view from five observed views and information about the component shapes. The benchmark contains 602 synthetic polycube assemblies with 2--10 parts and requires a dense grid of part labels for the missing view, allowing both exact-view and cell-level evaluation. For each item, we exhaustively verify that all legal assemblies consistent with the exact component geometry and observed label grids yield the same target view. With these inputs, the task tests symbolic assembly and coordinate reasoning. The image-only variants additionally require shape recovery from rendered views, where occlusion can make different 3D shapes look identical. We evaluate three vision-language models under four input conditions. Across 552 items with complete evaluations, exact-grid accuracy with images plus exact text ranges from 33.2% to 85.4%. Adding exact text to separate images improves accuracy by 19.7--63.0 percentage points, whereas adding images to exact text changes it by only $-0.5$ to $+2.1$ points. Separate image panels outperform a merged sheet by 6.7--11.1 points. The results show that performance depends strongly on access to exact symbolic information, with little further improvement from images once the geometry is specified. GitHub: https://github.com/facebookresearch/sixthview_benchmark

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SixthView，一个从五个正交视图与部件形状信息预测隐藏第六视图的基准，包含 602 个合成 polycube 装配，并支持精确视图与单元级评估；同时评测三个 VLM 在四种输入条件下的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接考察遮挡与几何装配推理，且发现图像在给定精确文本后增益很小、分图优于拼图，可供核查 VLM 是否真正使用视觉证据、以及视觉信息被符号输入旁路的假设，但与 latent 状态生成无直接关系。
